name: Cubical geometry proves the virtual Haken conjecture
summary: Wise's special cube complexes and Agol's criterion show that hyperbolic 3-manifold groups are virtually special, giving virtual Haken and virtual fibring.

name: Relative Langlands duality and electromagnetic duality
summary: Periods and L-functions were indexed by dual Hamiltonian spaces, guided by electromagnetic duality in physics, to extend the Langlands correspondence between periods and L-functions in both directions.

name: Random hyperbolic surfaces have maximal spectral gap: random-graph technique transfer
summary: Friedman's method for handling problematic paths in random graphs was adapted to hyperbolic surfaces and Mirzakhani-style geodesic counts to prove the optimal spectral gap of 1/4 for random surfaces.

name: Dynamical systems and spectral theory of Schrodinger operators
summary: Renormalisation and cocycle dynamics are used to describe the spectrum of quasi-periodic Schrodinger operators, solving the Ten Martini type problems.

name: Approximate groups and the model theory of pseudofinite structures
summary: A Lie-model theorem built with nonstandard methods describes the structure of finite approximate subgroups.

name: Amplituhedron: scattering amplitudes as volumes in positive geometry
summary: Recursion relations for gluon amplitudes were shown to compute volumes of pieces of the positive Grassmannian, and amplitudes were then proposed to be the volume of a new geometric object.

name: Inverse theorem for Gowers norms and Mobius-nilsequences
to: analytic number theory (linear equations in primes)
summary: Green-Tao-Ziegler proved nilsequences control Gowers norms, settling linear equations in primes counts.

name: Algorithmic discrepancy theory (Bansal) and the Komlos conjecture
summary: Designing efficient vector-balancing algorithms, rather than existence arguments, turned out to reproduce and then improve the best known discrepancy bounds, including a new bound towards Komlos.

name: Fargues-Scholze geometrisation of the local Langlands correspondence
summary: The Fargues-Fontaine curve and Scholze's diamonds were used to turn representations of Galois groups and of p-adic groups into sheaves, proving one direction of local Langlands.

name: Umbral moonshine and pariah moonshine
summary: Mathieu moonshine and 23 further umbral moonshines link groups to mock modular forms, proved in 2015, and a pariah group (O'Nan) was tied to weight-3/2 modular forms in 2017.
